paragraphs: Running a neural network across several devices requires deciding where each mathematical operation should execute. The paper treats this as a problem on a computation graph, whose directed connections describe dependencies between operations. Its framework combines ideas from methods that group operations before assigning devices and methods that learn graph representations before making assignments.

The framework uses smaller computation graphs extracted from OpenVINO and includes graph coarsening, learning node representations, and policy optimization among its five steps. It supports training the whole system together while accounting for the graph's directed, acyclic structure. A further model variant learns representations and customized graph partitions jointly, without requiring a fixed number of groups. Reinforcement learning uses placement execution time to guide training.

Experiments cover Inception-V3, ResNet, and BERT, with an ablation study examining robustness. The proposed placements improve inference speed by up to 58.2% over CPU execution and up to 60.24% over commonly used baselines. These are reported best-case improvements across the evaluated settings, showing the practical value of incorporating graph structure into placement decisions.
neurips-2024-a-structure-aware-framework.tldr: A graph-aware learning framework assigns neural-network operations to devices and reports substantial inference-speed improvements on three benchmark models.

paragraphs: This paper studies the best achievable prediction error when learning a particular random neural network: one hidden layer with quadratic activations. The analysis takes a large-system limit in which input dimension and network width grow proportionally. Its focus is the regime where the number of training examples grows quadratically with input dimension, extending an earlier result for only linearly many examples.

The authors derive a closed-form expression for the Bayes-optimal test error in this setting. They also introduce GAMP-RIE, which combines approximate message passing with rotationally invariant matrix denoising and asymptotically attains that performance. The mathematical connection to extensive-rank matrix denoising and ellipsoid fitting makes the neural-network learning problem accessible through related estimation problems.

A separate empirical finding concerns gradient descent without observation noise. Random initializations appear to produce different weight solutions with zero training loss, while averaging their predictions yields test error matching the Bayes-optimal value. This observation is presented as empirical evidence, distinct from the asymptotic optimality result for GAMP-RIE, and applies to the studied quadratic-network setting.
neurips-2024-bayes-optimal-learning-of-a.tldr: For a large random network with quadratic activations, the paper derives Bayes-optimal test error and an algorithm that asymptotically achieves it.

paragraphs: BuckTales provides annotated aerial footage for following individual blackbuck antelopes in their natural habitat. The animals are recorded during mating behavior known as lekking, making the footage relevant to biological questions about social behavior. The dataset addresses a shortage of wild-animal data that has constrained automated tracking research despite increasing access to drones.

Its tracking portion contains more than 1.2 million annotations and 680 tracks across 12 high-resolution 5.4K videos. Each video averages 66 seconds and includes between 30 and 130 animals. A separate re-identification portion contains 730 individuals recorded simultaneously with two drones. Tracking follows animals through footage, while re-identification concerns recognizing the same individual across observations.

Developed with biologists, the dataset connects computer-vision evaluation with ecologically meaningful monitoring. The authors provide baseline results using two detectors and evaluate several established tracking methods. The contribution is a shared resource for studying the challenges of natural settings; scalable, long-term monitoring and resulting conservation insights are goals the dataset is intended to support.
neurips-2024-bucktales-a-multi-uav-datas.tldr: BuckTales supplies annotated multi-drone footage of wild blackbuck antelopes to support animal tracking and re-identification research.

paragraphs: Croissant addresses the practical friction of finding and using datasets across different machine-learning tools. The paper introduces a shared metadata format: a common way to describe datasets so repositories, frameworks, and platforms can work with the same representation. Its contribution concerns the information surrounding a dataset and how that information supports access and use.

A shared description helps make datasets discoverable, portable, and interoperable. These goals connect different parts of the workflow: locating suitable data, moving between tools, and loading data into a framework. The paper reports support from several popular repositories spanning hundreds of thousands of datasets, with loading into commonly used machine-learning frameworks regardless of where the data is stored.

The authors also report an initial human evaluation of the metadata itself. Raters found the descriptions readable, understandable, complete, and concise. That finding matters because the format is intended to serve people as well as software. Together, repository support and the initial evaluation provide evidence for Croissant's practical role as shared infrastructure for dataset use.
neurips-2024-croissant-a-metadata-format.tldr: Croissant standardizes dataset metadata to make machine-learning data easier to discover, move between tools, and load.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to represent a set of k items from a large universe while satisfying differential privacy. The central challenge is to balance privacy, representation error, storage, and computation. Its constructions embed sets into random linear systems, taking a different route from approaches that add noise to an otherwise non-private representation.

The first construction satisfies approximate differential privacy, parameterized by epsilon and delta. It achieves error probability 1/(e^epsilon + 1), with storage at most 1.05 k epsilon log(e) bits. Construction takes O(k log(1/delta)) time, and decoding takes O(log(1/delta)) time. A second construction achieves pure epsilon differential privacy with the same error and a smaller stated storage bound of k epsilon log(e) bits, but requires large decoding times.

The privacy–utility trade-offs match lower bounds, including constants while disregarding delta factors. The authors also establish a storage lower bound that matches their constructions within small constant factors. These results characterize how compact private set representations can be, while the two algorithms expose a practical trade-off between the privacy guarantee, storage, and decoding effort.
neurips-2024-differentially-private-set-.tldr: Random linear-system constructions yield compact private set representations with near-matching storage lower bounds and sharp privacy–error trade-offs.

paragraphs: FedLPA addresses federated learning with just one round of communication between clients and a server. Each client trains on its own data, and the server must combine the resulting models into a useful global model. This becomes difficult when clients have substantially different data distributions, because their locally trained models reflect different statistical patterns.

The method summarizes each local model layer using a Laplace approximation to its posterior distribution. This provides a probabilistic description of the layer's parameters and captures information associated with the client's data. FedLPA then aggregates these layer-level posteriors to train the global parameters. The approach does not require an additional auxiliary dataset or disclosure of private label information such as each client's label distribution.

The authors report significant learning-performance improvements over state-of-the-art methods across several metrics in extensive experiments. The contribution is therefore a way to make a single aggregation round more informative under heterogeneous data. Its stated privacy-related benefit is avoiding the specified extra disclosures; the abstract does not present that benefit as a formal privacy guarantee.
neurips-2024-fedlpa-one-shot-federated-l.tldr: FedLPA combines layer-level posterior approximations to improve one-shot federated learning when clients have different data distributions.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether contaminating training data alone can compromise a diffusion model. Earlier attacks discussed in the abstract also required changes to diffusion training or sampling procedures. Here, the authors study a BadNets-like setting in which those procedures remain unchanged, isolating the effect of poisoned examples in the dataset.

They find that this form of poisoning can make generated images disagree with their intended text conditions. They also observe trigger amplification: triggers appear at an increased rate among generated images. That second effect has a defensive use, because the amplified presence of triggers can help reveal poisoned training data. The same phenomenon therefore connects generation failures with a possible detection strategy.

The authors further investigate how studying poisoned diffusion models can inform robust image-classifier design, including when the poisoning ratio is low. They also link poisoning effects with data replication by examining diffusion models' tendency to memorize training data. The findings establish both an attack surface and opportunities for defense, rather than treating poisoned generation solely as a failure to prevent.
neurips-2024-from-trojan-horses-to-castl.tldr: Training-data poisoning can misdirect diffusion models, while their amplification of attack triggers can also help detect poisoning.

paragraphs: Experiments become harder to interpret when treating one participant changes other participants' outcomes. These spillovers can occur through direct or indirect interactions, and the interaction network may be unknown. The paper develops treatment-effect estimators for this setting, aiming to recover how the total effect evolves over time despite pervasive interference.

The proposed causal message-passing approach uses the sample means and variances of treatments and outcomes over time. It constructs nonlinear features from these statistical moments and learns a function that predicts future outcome means and variances. This gives a model of the system's evolving state from which treatment-effect dynamics can be estimated, using observed aggregate information when the interaction structure is unknown.

Simulations across multiple domains, with both synthetic and real network data, demonstrate effective estimation of total treatment-effect dynamics. The reported results include cases where interference varies non-monotonically with treatment probability, so increasing treatment probability does not produce a simple one-directional pattern. The work offers an empirical basis for studying complex spillovers through their time-dependent statistical consequences.
neurips-2024-higher-order-causal-message.tldr: A causal message-passing estimator uses evolving treatment and outcome statistics to estimate treatment effects under unknown, complex interference.

paragraphs: The paper develops a learned dynamics model that makes established control methods usable in a low-dimensional latent space. It identifies three obstacles in existing models: missing physical structure, lack of inherent stability preservation, and difficulty translating desired latent forces into actual control inputs. Coupled Oscillator Networks, or CONs, are designed to address these obstacles together.

The authors analytically show that CON has a Lagrangian structure with defined kinetic and potential energies. They also prove global input-to-state stability using Lyapunov arguments, connecting the model's stability to its inputs. An approximate closed-form integration method supports efficient training. To translate latent forces into controls, a decoder learns to reconstruct inputs from encoded forces; this mapping is approximated rather than established as exactly invertible.

Experiments report state-of-the-art performance when learning complex nonlinear mechanical dynamics directly from images. The authors then combine the model with an integral-saturated PID controller and potential-force compensation. They demonstrate high-quality control of a soft robot using only raw pixels as feedback, connecting the model's mathematical structure with a concrete control application.
neurips-2024-input-to-state-stable-coupl.tldr: Coupled Oscillator Networks combine physical structure and proven stability with learned input decoding to enable latent-space robot control from images.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning from human feedback trains a language model using a learned reward model as a proxy for human preferences. Optimizing that proxy too aggressively can create overoptimization: improvement according to the reward model can become an unreliable guide to the intended objective. This paper addresses the problem by estimating how trustworthy the reward signal is.

The uncertainty method uses only embeddings from the reward model's last layer. This restriction is central to its lightweight design, allowing the method to assess reward reliability from a limited part of the model's representation. The authors then use that uncertainty estimate in AdvPO, a distributionally robust optimization procedure designed to mitigate reward overoptimization during RLHF.

Experiments on Anthropic HH and TL;DR summarization report that AdvPO reduces overoptimization and improves RLHF performance under human-assisted evaluation. The result supports using reward uncertainty as part of the training objective, so the optimization procedure accounts for the proxy's reliability. The paper's stated finding is mitigation in these evaluations, rather than complete removal of reward-model error.
neurips-2024-mitigating-reward-overoptim.tldr: AdvPO uses lightweight reward uncertainty estimates to mitigate overoptimization and improve human-assisted evaluations of RLHF-trained models.

paragraphs: Algorithmic monoculture occurs when many decision-makers use the same algorithm to evaluate applicants. The paper studies its consequences in a two-sided matching market, where outcomes depend jointly on applicants' preferences and decision-makers' evaluations. This market perspective matters because changing evaluations can also change who competes for whom and which matches ultimately form.

The authors introduce a tractable theoretical model comparing a shared evaluation algorithm with independent evaluations, called polyculture. Holding other factors equal, monoculture selects applicants who are less preferred by decision-makers when evaluation noise is well-behaved. At the same time, it matches more applicants to their top choice. These results show that decision-maker selection quality and applicant choice satisfaction can move in different directions.

The increase in top-choice matches does not mean every applicant benefits. Individual outcomes depend on applicants' value to decision-makers and their tolerance for risk. The model also finds monoculture more robust to differences in the number of applications submitted. Together, the findings characterize several distinct consequences of shared evaluation, rather than assigning it a single market-wide benefit or harm.
neurips-2024-monoculture-in-matching-mar.tldr: A matching-market model shows that shared evaluation algorithms can worsen selection quality while increasing top-choice matches and robustness to application-count disparities.

paragraphs: The paper investigates why contrastive learning across two modalities can produce better representations than learning from one modality alone. Its aim is to explain differences in feature learning and downstream performance within a shared theoretical framework. This connects the empirical success of language-supervised multimodal learning to an analysis of what training actually learns.

The analysis assumes a data-generation model with signal and noise and studies a ReLU network trained using an InfoMax objective. By following the optimization trajectory and characterizing downstream generalization, the authors identify signal-to-noise ratio as a critical factor for both single-modal and multimodal learning. This makes the quality of the available signal central to understanding the comparison.

Within the framework, cooperation between modalities can improve learned features and thereby improve downstream-task performance. The claim is an explanation of how multimodal gains can arise under the analyzed setting, rather than a universal advantage for every pair of modalities. Experiments using synthetic and real-world datasets support the theoretical findings, linking the analysis to observed learning behavior.
neurips-2024-on-the-comparison-between-m.tldr: A feature-learning analysis identifies signal-to-noise ratio as central to when cooperation between modalities can improve contrastive learning.

paragraphs: This paper studies a concrete form of in-context learning: predicting a test example's label by finding its nearest labeled example in the prompt. The prompt contains labeled training data together with unlabeled test data. The question is whether training can make a very small transformer learn this one-nearest-neighbor rule and then apply it through its context.

Under the paper's theoretical framework, gradient descent can train a single softmax attention layer to behave like a one-nearest-neighbor classifier. The result concerns successful learning despite a nonconvex loss function, meaning the training objective does not have a simple globally bowl-shaped geometry. It therefore addresses the optimization process as well as the behavior the trained layer can express.

The finding gives a concrete example of a transformer learning to implement a nonparametric prediction algorithm. Task-specific examples supplied in the prompt provide the information used for prediction, which helps explain how context can support new tasks without further fine-tuning. The result also clarifies a role for softmax attention within this particular theoretical setting.
neurips-2024-one-layer-transformer-prova.tldr: Under a theoretical framework, gradient descent trains one softmax attention layer to perform one-nearest-neighbor classification from examples in its prompt.

paragraphs: The paper studies RLHF when preference feedback need not come from an underlying reward function. Many prior approaches assume preferences follow a Bradley–Terry model built from such rewards. Here, the authors allow a more general preference oracle, broadening the kinds of feedback relationships the learning framework can represent.

They formulate learning as a reverse-KL-regularized minimax game between two language models. The objective is to find a policy that the regularized preference oracle consistently prefers over competing policies. This expresses the target directly through comparisons between models, with KL regularization included in the formulation. The authors show that this framework is strictly more general than the reward-based one.

The paper proposes sample-efficient algorithms for two data-access settings. Offline learning uses an already collected preference dataset, while online learning queries the preference oracle during training. Empirical studies support the framework's effectiveness. The contribution combines a broader mathematical account of preferences with learning procedures for both fixed data and continuing feedback, making the general formulation operational in both settings.
neurips-2024-online-iterative-reinforcem.tldr: A preference-game formulation broadens RLHF beyond reward-based assumptions and supports sample-efficient offline and online learning algorithms.

paragraphs: This paper addresses adapting pretrained models when data is distributed across clients with strongly different local distributions. In that federated setting, the authors argue that fine-tuning the entire model is ineffective under diverse data skew. They instead optimize a small collection of input prefixes, or prompts, that modify how the pretrained model behaves.

The approach treats federated learning as distributed set modeling. Clients contribute diverse sets of prompts, and aggregation combines those sets to adapt the model globally. The paper benchmarks direct adaptations of existing federated model-aggregation techniques, then introduces a probabilistic prompt-aggregation method. This changes the object being combined from a full model to collections of prompts learned from different local data.

Results across several computer-vision datasets show that the probabilistic method substantially outperforms the evaluated aggregation baselines. The authors report that it is most effective against extreme data heterogeneity. The findings support prompt-set aggregation as a useful way to handle strongly skewed federated data, with the empirical advantage tied to the tested datasets and comparisons.
neurips-2024-probabilistic-federated-pro.tldr: Probabilistic aggregation of locally learned prompt sets improves federated model adaptation, especially under extreme data heterogeneity in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: The paper studies online matching when arrival distributions are known and stationary. Its objective is to maximize the lowest matching rate across arriving types, giving priority to long-run fairness. This differs from maximizing the total number served: a high overall match count can coexist with a low service rate for some types.

With one offline agent, first-come-first-served matches the optimal clairvoyant performance for this objective. For the general problem, the authors introduce SAMP and prove competitiveness of at least 1−1/e. Its competitiveness approaches one in specified regimes: sufficiently large capacity for every offline agent, sufficiently high arrival rates for every online type, or strong imbalance between total capacity and arrivals.

The paper also establishes worst-case limits: non-rejecting policies cannot exceed 1/2 competitiveness, arbitrary randomized policies cannot exceed √3−1, and SAMP cannot exceed 1−1/e. The authors describe these hardness results as independent of benchmark choice. Thus, SAMP's general bound is tight even though its performance approaches optimality in special regimes. Extensions address group-level and short-run fairness with further provable algorithms.
neurips-2024-promoting-fairness-among-dy.tldr: SAMP provides provable long-run fairness guarantees for online matching and approaches optimality under specified capacity or arrival regimes.

paragraphs: Generative Flow Networks generate combinatorial objects with the aim of obtaining both useful and diverse samples. A practical challenge is steering them more consistently toward high-utility outputs. This paper studies how to make their sampling behavior greedier while retaining the variety that makes these generative methods valuable.

QGFN combines a GFlowNet's sampling policy with an action-value estimate, called Q, drawing on connections with reinforcement learning. The value estimate supplies an additional signal about the utility associated with actions. A mixing parameter controls how the two ingredients contribute, giving a way to adjust the sampling policy's degree of greediness. The paper examines several variants of this combined approach.

Across a variety of tasks, several QGFN variants generate more high-reward samples without sacrificing diversity. This is an empirical result for the evaluated variants and tasks. Its significance is that stronger emphasis on utility need not erase diversity in those settings: the combined policy offers a controllable way to improve the useful portion of generated samples.
neurips-2024-qgfn-controllable-greedines.tldr: QGFN mixes GFlowNet policies with action-value estimates to generate more high-reward samples while preserving diversity in the reported tasks.

paragraphs: Fine-tuned vision-language models can learn misleading associations between visual features and textual attributes. Such associations may hurt zero-shot classification at test time. RaVL addresses this problem at the level of local image regions, aiming to identify the particular visual features involved in errors and then change how the model uses them.

The discovery stage clusters image regions to locate features contributing to zero-shot classification mistakes. The mitigation stage introduces a region-aware loss for fine-tuning, encouraging attention to relevant regions and discouraging the identified spurious relationships. Connecting these stages makes the discovered local features directly relevant to the corrective training procedure, rather than diagnosing the problem only at whole-image level.

The evaluation spans 654 vision-language models with different architectures, data domains, and learned spurious correlations. The authors report a 191% improvement over the closest baseline in discovering these correlations and an 8.2% improvement in worst-group classification accuracy after mitigation. Qualitative evaluations in general and medical domains further support the findings, providing evidence for the usefulness of region-level diagnosis and correction.
neurips-2024-ravl-discovering-and-mitiga.tldr: RaVL identifies misleading image-region associations and uses a region-aware training loss to improve vision-language model robustness.

paragraphs: Closed-loop neuroscience experiments use recorded neural activity to change an experiment while it is running. Calcium-imaging videos can support this process, but extracting individual neurons' activity often requires batch analysis. Streaming analysis must also handle dim neurons and avoid attributing signals from undiscovered neurons to cells already being tracked.

realSEUDO adapts the SEUDO time-trace estimator into an online algorithm that identifies neurons and estimates their activity simultaneously. It is designed to remain robust to neurons that have not yet been identified. Algorithmic improvements, a fast C implementation, and a new cell-finding loop allow new cells to be discovered during processing without a warm-up period.

The authors report performance comparable to offline methods such as CNMF and better than the online approach OnACID. Average processing speed reaches 120 Hz, exceeding the typical 30 Hz imaging rate. That speed difference matters because a closed-loop experiment must also compute its feedback response. The reported performance therefore addresses both signal-extraction quality and the time needed to act on the resulting activity estimates.
neurips-2024-realseudo-for-real-time-cal.tldr: realSEUDO identifies neurons and estimates their activity from streaming calcium-imaging video fast enough to leave time for experimental feedback.

paragraphs: Evaluating videos generated from text remains difficult even as generation capabilities improve. Automatic metrics have limitations, making human assessment an important evaluation method. However, human judgments are only useful as a shared measure when the evaluation process is reliable, reproducible, and practical to run. This paper focuses on improving that process.

The authors introduce Text-to-Video Human Evaluation, or T2VHE, as a standardized protocol. It combines clearly defined evaluation metrics, thorough training for annotators, and a dynamic evaluation module. These components make the evaluation procedure itself part of the contribution: they specify what is judged, prepare the people making judgments, and organize how evaluation proceeds.

Experiments show that the protocol produces high-quality annotations and can reduce evaluation costs by nearly 50%. The cost finding accompanies the quality result, addressing the practical burden of manual assessment. The authors state plans to release the workflow, dynamic evaluation details, and annotation-interface code. Sharing that setup is intended to help other groups establish more developed and reproducible human-assessment procedures.
neurips-2024-rethinking-human-evaluation.tldr: T2VHE standardizes human evaluation of text-generated videos and reports high-quality annotations with nearly 50% lower evaluation costs.

paragraphs: SceneCraft generates indoor 3D scenes from both textual descriptions and user-specified spatial layouts. The paper targets complex spaces whose arrangement matters, extending beyond the small scenes and restricted shape or texture control described for earlier text-to-3D methods. Its input gives users a way to specify both scene content and spatial organization.

The method first renders a 3D semantic layout into 2D proxy maps from multiple viewpoints. A diffusion model conditioned on semantic and depth information uses those maps to generate multi-view images. These images then supervise a neural radiance field, or NeRF, which becomes the final scene representation. The sequence connects explicit layout guidance with image generation and a learned 3D representation.

Because the method is not constrained by panorama generation, it supports spaces beyond a single room, including irregular multi-bedroom apartments. Experimental comparisons report significant improvements over existing approaches in generating complex interiors with varied textures, consistent geometry, and realistic appearance. The contribution combines user control over arrangement with the ability to represent more complicated indoor environments.
neurips-2024-scenecraft-layout-guided-3d.tldr: SceneCraft turns text and spatial layouts into detailed 3D interiors through layout-conditioned multi-view image generation and NeRF learning.

paragraphs: Video language models face a tension between retaining detailed information within frames and sampling enough frames to understand events over time. SlowFocus addresses this by concentrating temporal detail where a question makes it most relevant. The goal is finer understanding of video events without reducing the quality of each frame's visual-token representation.

The mechanism first identifies the temporal segment related to the question. It then samples that segment densely to extract local high-frequency information. A multi-frequency mixing attention module combines those details with more sparsely sampled global context. This allows the model to use both a close temporal view of the relevant event and broader information about the surrounding video.

The authors introduce training strategies for locating relevant time segments and reasoning about temporal details. They also create FineAction-CGR to evaluate fine-grained temporal understanding. Experiments report superior performance across existing public video-understanding benchmarks and the new benchmark. The findings support question-guided allocation of temporal sampling as a way to improve detailed comprehension while preserving frame-level information.
neurips-2024-slowfocus-enhancing-fine-gr.tldr: SlowFocus densely samples question-relevant video segments and combines them with global context to improve fine-grained temporal understanding.

paragraphs: Inverse problems recover underlying information from incomplete or degraded measurements, such as reconstructing a clean image from a poor signal. Diffusion models offer useful reconstruction capabilities, but the paper argues that existing approaches often simplify the problem to a linear setting. Such simplifications can contribute to accumulated errors and biases when degradation is more complex.

The authors analyze stochastic-differential-equation diffusion models through random dynamical systems. Their framework uses measure-preserving dynamics to examine temporal distribution discrepancy, connecting the evolution of distributions with reconstruction stability. From this analysis, they identify strategies for improving stability and generalizability and introduce a score-based model called the Dynamics-aware SDE Diffusion Generative Model, or D^3GM.

The paper argues that the measure-preserving property, together with the random-dynamical-system notion of stability, can support returning degraded measurements to their original state under complex degradation. Experiments across multiple benchmarks, including magnetic resonance imaging, corroborate D^3GM's effectiveness. The contribution links a dynamical explanation of reconstruction difficulties to a model designed around that explanation and evaluated on inverse-problem applications.
neurips-2024-stability-and-generalizabil.tldr: D^3GM uses a random-dynamical-systems framework to improve diffusion reconstruction stability and generalizability under complex degradation.

paragraphs: SWT-Bench evaluates whether language-model code agents can turn user-reported software issues into executable tests. The benchmark draws on popular GitHub repositories and combines real issues with ground-truth fixes and reference tests. This makes the task a concrete assessment of whether an agent can formalize the behavior described in a bug report.

The authors find that language models generally generate relevant tests well, and that agents designed for code repair outperform systems designed specifically for test generation. They evaluate issue reproduction and changes in coverage, using these as complementary views of system behavior. Reproduction assesses whether a test captures the reported problem, while coverage changes describe how test execution exercises the code.

Generated tests also help screen proposed repairs. In the reported evaluation, using them as a filter doubles SWE-Agent's precision. This shows how test generation can contribute to the reliability of code-generation workflows as well as serve as an evaluation task itself. The authors release the benchmark's data and code to support further work on these uses.
neurips-2024-swt-bench-testing-and-valid.tldr: SWT-Bench evaluates issue-driven test generation and shows that generated tests can improve the precision of proposed bug fixes.

paragraphs: TAPVid-3D provides a benchmark for tracking individual points through real-world video in three dimensions over long time spans. The paper identifies a gap between established 2D point-tracking benchmarks and the absence of a corresponding real-world benchmark for 3D tracking. Its contribution creates a shared basis for measuring progress on that harder task.

Built from existing footage, the benchmark contains more than 4,000 videos from three data sources. These cover varied objects, motions, and indoor and outdoor environments. Its metrics extend a Jaccard-based measure used in 2D tracking to account for ambiguous depth scales across models, occlusion, and the spatial and temporal smoothness of multiple tracks.

The authors manually check a large sample of trajectories for annotation correctness and construct competitive baselines from existing tracking models. These steps connect the dataset to both annotation validation and an assessment of current methods. The intended longer-term role is to guide progress in understanding precise 3D motion and surface deformation from monocular video, with benchmark construction providing the foundation for that work.
neurips-2024-tapvid-3d-a-benchmark-for-t.tldr: TAPVid-3D introduces over 4,000 real-world videos and tailored metrics for evaluating long-range 3D point tracking.
